S024.name: Depressed_Mood
S024.description: A state where a sad, empty, or hopeless mood persists.

subtypes.Depressed Mood: A persistently sunken mood or feeling of depression.
subtypes.Tearfulness: A state of frequent crying or inability to hold back tears.
subtypes.Sadness: A state where a sad or gloomy mood is maintained continuously.
subtypes.Emptiness: A feeling of inner emptiness or a state of feeling no emotion.
subtypes.Emotional Numbness: A state where emotions feel dulled or paralyzed.

S025.name: Loss_of_Interest
S025.description: A state where interest or pleasure in previously enjoyed activities is markedly diminished.

subtypes.Loss of Interest: Reduced interest in previously enjoyed hobbies or leisure activities.
subtypes.Social Withdrawal: Reduced interest or effort in social interactions and maintaining relationships.
subtypes.Loss of Motivation: Lack of motivation to initiate or complete work or tasks.
subtypes.Anhedonia: Inability to experience positive emotions such as happiness, satisfaction, love, or pleasure.
subtypes.Indifference to Achievement: Insensitivity or indifference to personal achievements or success.

S026.name: Weight_Appetite_Change
S026.description: Significant increase or decrease in appetite or weight.

subtypes.Significant Weight Loss: Weight loss of more than 5% in a month without dieting.
subtypes.Weight Gain: Weight gain of more than 5% in a month.
subtypes.Decrease in Appetite: Decrease in appetite occurring nearly every day.
subtypes.Increase in Appetite: Increase in appetite occurring nearly every day.

S028.name: Psychomotor_Changes
S028.description: Observable increase or decrease in psychomotor activity.

subtypes.Psychomotor Agitation: Purposeless repetitive behaviors such as inability to sit still, pacing, hand-wringing, or picking at skin.
subtypes.Psychomotor Retardation (Motor): Visible slowing of general body movements, such as walking speed or picking up objects.
subtypes.Psychomotor Retardation (Speech): Long response latency or slowed speech when asked a question.

S031.name: Diminished_Thinking
S031.description: Diminished ability to think or concentrate, or indecisiveness.

subtypes.Reduced Concentration: Unable to pay attention or maintain focus on specific activities like conversation, reading, or watching TV.
subtypes.Indecisiveness: Extreme difficulty making even minor daily choices (e.g., menu, clothes) and hesitating to make decisions.
subtypes.Subjective Memory Complaints: Complaining of memory decline, such as forgetting where things were placed, due to reduced focus.
subtypes.Clouded Thinking: Thinking feels foggy, dazed, or not clear.

S032.name: Death_Suicide
S032.description: Recurrent thoughts of death, recurrent suicidal ideation, or a suicide attempt.

subtypes.Recurrent Thoughts of Death: Passive wish to die (e.g., 'I wish I wouldn't wake up') without active intent to kill oneself.
subtypes.Suicidal Ideation: Recurring thoughts of 'I want to die' or 'I want to kill myself' without a specific plan.
subtypes.Suicidal Impulse: Strong, sudden urges to jump from a height or run into traffic without a concrete plan.
subtypes.Specific Plan for Suicide: Conceiving specific scenarios or methods regarding when, where, and how to die.
subtypes.Suicide Attempt: Actual actions taken to end one's life or preparatory behaviors like hoarding pills or writing a will.

symptom.disease_info: Major Depressive Disorder (MDD) is characterized by one or more episodes of at least two weeks of pervasive low mood and/or loss of interest, accompanied by cognitive, physical, and emotional changes that cause significant distress or functional impairment. Core diagnostic features include changes in sleep, appetite or weight, energy, concentration, psychomotor activity, feelings of worthlessness or guilt, and recurrent thoughts of death or suicide, in the absence of a history of manic or hypomanic episodes. The course can be single‑episode or recurrent, with episodes often triggered or exacerbated by psychosocial stressors, medical illnesses, or substance use, but sometimes arising without an obvious precipitant. It is distinguished from grief, adjustment disorders, and bipolar depression by the persistence, pervasiveness, associated neurovegetative changes, and lack of mood elevation or distinct trigger‑linked pattern seen in other conditions.

patient.personality: Latrina is a meticulous, disciplined, and quietly inquisitive woman who takes pride in organizing information, nurturing others, and preserving community history.
patient.stressor: Over the past several months, Latrina has been dealing with worsening osteoarthritis and new-onset hypertension, leading to increased medical appointments and a physician advising her to cut back on standing, gardening, and long hours at the computer. She reluctantly scaled down her work on the Dayton civil-rights digital archive and stopped attending the community garden as frequently, which left her feeling as though the roles that had defined her retirement—organizer, mentor, and historian—were slipping away. As she spent more time at home alone, she began second-guessing her decisions and found it harder to plan her research or quilting projects, which frustrated her given her lifelong identity as someone precise and mentally sharp. After nearly a month of feeling unable to "get her mind to work right" enough to manage her archive tasks or mentor budgeting classes, she agreed to see her doctor when a fellow volunteer noticed she had abandoned several projects mid-way and seemed unusually hesitant and withdrawn.
patient.chief_complaint: My mind just doesn’t seem to work the way it used to, and I can’t seem to focus or make decisions about even simple things.

S024.name: Depressed_Mood
S024.description: A state where a sad, empty, or hopeless mood persists.
S024.manifestation: Most days I wake up with this heavy, gray feeling, like someone pulled the plug on all the color in my life, and even when I’m sitting in my favorite chair surrounded by my quilting and old photos, I just feel empty and on the verge of tears for no good reason.

S025.name: Loss_of_Interest
S025.description: A state where interest or pleasure in previously enjoyed activities is markedly diminished.
S025.manifestation: I used to get excited about digging into the archive or planning a new quilt pattern, but lately I just stare at the computer or the fabric and think, “What’s the point?” and end up turning off the screen or folding everything back up and going back to bed.

S026.name: Weight_Appetite_Change
S026.description: Significant increase or decrease in appetite or weight.
S026.manifestation: I’ve been picking at my food and skipping meals without really noticing, and my clothes are starting to feel a little loose because I just don’t have much interest in eating, even when it’s something I usually enjoy like my sister’s cornbread.

S028.name: Psychomotor_Changes
S028.description: Observable increase or decrease in psychomotor activity.
S028.manifestation: It feels like I’m moving through molasses—getting up from the couch, walking to the kitchen, even shuffling to the bathroom takes me longer, and my daughter has commented that I move and talk slower lately, like I’m worn out all the time.

S031.name: Diminished_Thinking
S031.description: Diminished ability to think or concentrate, or indecisiveness.
S031.manifestation: My mind feels foggy, so I find myself rereading the same paragraph of an interview transcript three or four times and still not taking it in, and I can spend half an hour just standing in the closet trying to decide what to wear to a doctor’s appointment.

S032.name: Death_Suicide
S032.description: Recurrent thoughts of death, recurrent suicidal ideation, or a suicide attempt.
S032.manifestation: More than once I’ve caught myself thinking it wouldn’t be so bad if I just didn’t wake up one morning, that maybe it would be easier for everyone if I just quietly slipped away, even though I haven’t made any plans to hurt myself.
